title: Meta faces additional $567 million fine in biggest child safety ruling
subtitle: The new order adds to the $375 million already imposed, bringing the total to $942 million.
excerpt: Meta was ordered to pay $567 million, adding to the previous $375 million fine for a total of $942 million.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A court ruled that Meta must pay an additional $567 million fine, marking the largest penalty ever imposed in a child‑safety case involving a social network.

Details of the ruling

The ruling adds to the $375 million already established in a previous case, raising the total penalties to $942 million.

  • Additional fine: $567 million
  • Previous fine: $375 million
  • Cumulative total: $942 million

Fines of this magnitude are legal tools intended to reinforce compliance with online child‑protection standards. By imposing substantial amounts, courts aim to encourage companies to adopt preventive and corrective measures that reduce risks to children and teenagers.

Generally, judicial decisions involving child‑safety liability consider the severity of violations, the platform’s reach, and the potential harm to young users. The core goal is to ensure digital service providers create safe environments and respond effectively to incidents that may affect minors.

The total amount of $942 million represents the financial commitment required for Meta to adjust its practices and align with child‑protection requirements established by current law.

With information from BBC News.
